text: Bank of Israel Rejects Netanyahu's Proposal to Use Crypto to Evade Potential International Financial Sanctions According to the Financial Times, the Bank of Israel publicly rejected Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's proposal to use cryptocurrencies to circumvent potential international financial sanctions. On October 24, the central bank stated that crypto could not serve as a means of bypassing sanctions, urging the government to preserve economic ties with major trading partners and prevent further restrictions. In an October 23 television interview, Netanyahu warned that Israel could face international banking sanctions and said he had requested plans exploring alternative financial systems, including blockchain and cryptocurrencies. — link

text: Keystone Confirms Customer Data Exposure Following Unauthorized Website Access Keystone Hardware Wallet confirmed that a third party obtained customer shipping and order information following unauthorized access to its official website. The incident was detected on October 20, with the data exposure confirmed on October 23 after reviewing API activity with Shopify. Exposed information included names, contact details, shipping addresses, purchased items, and prices. Payment card and bank details, recovery phrases, private keys, and wallet passwords were not exposed. Keystone said it has blocked the access, fixed the vulnerability, and is notifying affected customers. It also warned of impersonation scams involving fake refunds, replacement devices, or order fixes. — link

text: Tokenized stocks are where stablecoins were many years ago: lots of issuers, split liquidity, and not much infra built to facilitate flows. To tap on the growing payments ecosystem. - Acceptance as collateral for perps, so you can trade on margin for improved capital efficiency. Stablecoins brought DeFi its first wave. Tokenized stocks will bring the next one.

text: Swell Pauses swETH and rswETH Deposits and Withdrawals Amid Abnormally High Contract Exchange Rates According to Unchained, Ethereum staking protocol Swell has paused deposits and withdrawals for swETH and rswETH until it corrects the net asset values (NAV) and exchange rates of both tokens. Data shows that the swETH and rswETH contracts reported exchange rates of approximately 1.203 ETH and 1.138 ETH, respectively, about 6% and 5% higher than normal levels. On-chain analyst Spreek suspected a compromise of the relevant token admin keys and identified a malicious upgrade contract that could potentially impact around 2,500 ETH, though the upgrade has not yet been executed. Swell stated that no ETH has been transferred out of the affected contracts and that the exact cause remains under investigation. — link

text: Highlight Clip: Arthur Hayes: High-FDV Shitcoins Can't Even Pump on Binance Anymore Arthur Hayes: High-FDV Shitcoins Can't Even Pump on Binance Anymore Flop Labs CEO Arthur Hayes said in an October 16 interview with LukeMartin that the entire crypto industry has abused tokenomics. From ICOs to VC private sales and presales, some projects raise funds supposedly to build products, only to dump tokens after launching protocols and unlocking allocations. Retail investors buying at TGE suffer heavy losses, sometimes watching token prices plunge 95%. Hayes argued that retail investors increasingly see through the high-FDV, low-float model, saying such tokens "can't even pump on Binance anymore." He favors projects like Hyperliquid, which have genuine product-market fit, return revenue to token holders, and avoid massive sell pressure from presold token unlocks. — link

text: Weekend reading. Courtesy of Paradis Labs - 1. J.P. Morgan — "Credit markets look for AI's weak links" (Oct 23, 2026) 2. George Hotz (@gdb) — "Towards Securing the Internet" 3. Aswath Damodaran — "From Eyeballs to Annual Run Rates (ARR): Buzzy Pricing Metrics and the Anthropic Trade!" 4. Neil Shah (Counterpoint) — "NVIDIA GTC Berlin 2026 – Containers, Safety and Sovereignty" Unfortunately UBS and Bernstein links are only for clients. Main takeaways. 1. Credit markets are now separating durable cash-flow generators from borrowers riding the AI narrative. 2. Manual, bug-by-bug handling won't scale in the agentic era. Brockman floats authorized internet-scale scanning, notification, and in extreme cases remote patching. He might be justifying a product line for OpenAI in cyber security. 3. ARR is the new eyeballs. non-standardized and gameable: OpenAI switched to net revenue, cutting reported ARR from 70B to50B, while Anthropic still books gross (cloud payments as expenses). Annualization window (day/week/month) is another lever 4. VC rounds are forward pricing, not value: Anthropic's May 2026 round raised 65B at965B post-money; OpenAI's March round 122B at852B, with a pending ~$1.4T round. Investors are discounting expected IPO pricing, a pure Keynesian beauty contest. 5. Jensen's push: Europe should produce AI, not just consume it. Especially on physical AI
